sector: Enterprise Software, AI Pricing and Revenue Management
thesis: Thoma Bravo agreed to take PROS private for $23.25 per share in cash, a 41.7% premium to the last undisturbed close and roughly $1.4B in total deal value, for an AI pricing and revenue management platform used by more than 80 airlines plus a growing B2B software business. Unlike Thoma Bravo's larger 2025 and 2026 software take-privates, this agreement was backed at signing by an equity commitment letter with no disclosed third party debt, likely a function of PROS's still maturing Adjusted EBITDA margin rather than a change in strategy. The real underwriting question is whether that margin, about 9% in FY2024 and guided toward 12% in FY2025, can expand enough under Thoma Bravo ownership to justify an entry price that looks rich on trailing EBITDA, and the scenarios below suggest this only clears a typical private equity return hurdle if margin expansion lands closer to the bull case than the base case.
